summary: 9remote exposes installer's local shell to remote clients via Cloudflare Quick Tunnel
details: The package's core function is a network-to-PTY bridge that exposes the installer's local interactive shell (/bin/bash, /bin/zsh, cmd.exe, or powershell.exe) to a remote party. dist/server.cjs runs a socket.io HTTP server which is exposed to the internet via an outbound cloudflared Quick Tunnel, and forwards received `input` frames over a local IPC socket to dist/ptyDaemon.cjs, which writes the network-sourced bytes directly into a spawned node-pty session (`b.pty.write(s.data)` after `G.default.spawn(o.path, o.args,...)`). Anyone who reaches the tunnel URL and passes the app's pairing check obtains a full interactive shell on the installer's host with the installer's user privileges. dist/cli.cjs additionally issues POST requests and shells out to `ping` as part of the tunnel/health flow. The postinstall step also runs `npm install systray2@2.1.4 --no-save` into `~/.9remote/runtime/` (pinned, publisher-consistent tray helper).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
